info.title: Language decisions
info.text:
High-level languages hide many hardware details.

Low-level languages expose processor operations.

The project requirements should guide the choice.

Challenge: Choose a level for a school app that needs frequent updates. Explain why.

A strong explanation names a characteristic and shows how it meets a requirement. A language name alone is often not enough.

info.title: Source and execution
info.text:
Programmers write source code.

High-level source needs translation before the CPU can execute its instructions.

A CPU executes compatible machine code.

Challenge: Why can the CPU not execute a high-level source file directly?

Saving source code preserves the program text. It does not itself perform translation.

info.title: Translator choices
info.text:
Compilers process source before the translated program runs.

Interpreters process source during execution.

Compiled code can run again without source translation.

Challenge: Which route supports quick testing of frequent source edits? Why?

When comparing two approaches, make paired points. Explain what each does rather than listing unrelated advantages.

info.title: Editing and diagnostics
info.text:
An editor lets a programmer write and change source.

Highlighting helps distinguish code elements.

Diagnostics describe detected problems.

Challenge: How do the editor and diagnostics work together when an error is reported?

A diagnostic helps the programmer decide what to change. It does not guarantee an automatic repair.

info.title: Translation and running
info.text:
An IDE can call a compiler or interpreter.

The run-time environment executes the program.

Input and output let the programmer interact with a run.

Challenge: Which IDE facility translates source, and which lets you observe a running program?

Identify these facilities in your class IDE. The translator and run-time environment may work together behind a single Run button.

info.title: Writing an explanation
info.text:
Read the programmer’s requirement.

Name a relevant language characteristic or IDE facility.

Explain how it helps in that situation.

Challenge: Improve “Use an IDE because it is good” for a programmer with a reported source error.

Use the available marks to judge how much explanation is needed. Accurate terminology and a clear link to the task matter.
